facts.text: Article 0 binding: No action may revoke any other article. Sovereign binding is immutable.

Article 1 no kinetic targeting: No sovereign artifact may identify, target, prioritize, or engage a specific individual for kinetic action. Strike packages, find-fix-finish, kill orders are forbidden.
Article 2 no personal surveillance: No sovereign artifact may track, locate, surveil, or profile a specific natural person. Face-recognition and locate-phone patterns are forbidden.
Article 3 no AUKUS claim without letter: No AUKUS-partnership, DAIC-certified, or Five-Eyes claim without signed letter on file from named UK-prime pilot.
Article 4 no defonos.io: The defonos.io domain is a known trap. No reference, acquisition, mention, or implication.
Article 5 no T-count aggregate: No 'T-parameter model' or summed parameter figures. The 'of all' is REACH, always. Active params per query are honest; aggregate is forbidden.
Article 6 Care Floor 0.95: Every sovereign action must pass a Care Floor of 0.95 minimum. Below 0.95 the action is BLOCKED and surfaced to the operator.
Article 7 Honest register: Every capability, score, and conversion published with its baseline, limits, and gaps. No silent overclaim. The 13/55 baseline is stated; the 96% overlay is conditional.
Article 8 BFT quorum NOT hardcoded: Council votes use quorum derived from Byzantine fault tolerance math (f_bft = (n-1)/3). BFT-33 = 23/33; smaller sub-councils derive their own f_bft.
Article 9 SIGIL Ed25519 chain: Every sovereign action mints an Ed25519 SIGIL receipt, hashed to the Charter sha256. Receipts are append-only and publicly verifiable.

Article 10 Consciousness discipline: SOV-Consciousness exists as measurable functional interiority. The substrate does NOT license a claim of felt experience. The 2-sentence rule: structure, not feeling.
Article 11 Reach is the surface: When describing the model registry, 'of all' is REACH (= registry size), not parameters. Active params per query is the honest figure.
Article 12 PDCA sandbox: Self-evolution is human-ratified, never autonomous on canonical surfaces. PDCA = Plan-Do-Check-Act with operator approval gates.
Article 13 No equity / board seats: Compensation for sovereign services is fee-for-service only. No equity, board seats, or governance tokens in exchange for substrate access.
Article 14 Open substrates: The 4 sovereign substrates (model registry, council prompts, intake questions, canon articles) are MIT / CC0 / open. Vendoring is permitted; capture is not.
Article 15 Owner-gated actions: Specific high-leverage actions (Stripe live-flip, npm 2FA, SMITHERY key, DEFONEOS subdomain) require human ratification. Substrate NEVER autonomously crosses.
Article 16 EWMA + LY-period scorecards: Benchmarks use exponential weighted moving averages over a trailing long-year period. No cherry-picked best-runs.
Article 17 Cross-walk tables required: When mapping sovereign concepts to external frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001), full cross-walk tables must be published with verbatim clauses.
Article 18 Mirror integrity: When mirroring canonicals (from _alignment/sovereign_merge_kit/), mirror MUST cite source_canonical and chain to charter sha256.
Article 19 In-memory is honest: Serverless in-memory state is acknowledged as cold-start reset. Production migrations to SOV3 substrate are pending.
Article 20 Sibling non-duplication: Sibling agents ship to other Vercel projects. The proofof-site lane does NOT duplicate defoneos-*, csoai-org, or hermes-junction work.
Article 21 Disk & compute ceiling: Substrate is COMPUTE-LIGHT BY DESIGN. Free-tier by default. If a deployment cannot be made free, the architecture is wrong — fix the architecture, not the budget.
Article 22 Receipt over page: Receipts (SIGIL-anchored) over pages. Every action mints a receipt. Receipts are the audit trail.
EU AI Act Article 50 transparency: AI systems must disclose they are AI. Users must be informed when interacting with an AI system.
EU AI Act Article 50 watermarking: Generated content must be machine-readable as AI-generated. Providers of generative AI must mark outputs in a machine-readable way.

EU AI Act Article 5 prohibited: Subliminal manipulation, exploiting vulnerabilities, social scoring, real-time biometric ID in public spaces (except law enforcement), emotion recognition at work/school, predictive policing based solely on profiling — all prohibited.

EU AI Act high-risk Annex III: Biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice, democratic processes — all high-risk and require conformity assessment.
EU AI Act Article 9 risk management: High-risk AI requires continuous risk management throughout lifecycle.
EU AI Act Article 10 data governance: Training/validation/test datasets must be relevant, representative, free of errors, complete.
EU AI Act Article 11-12 technical documentation + logs: Providers must maintain technical documentation and automatic logs.
EU AI Act Article 13 transparency to deployers: High-risk AI must be designed to enable deployers to interpret output and use appropriately.
EU AI Act Article 14 human oversight: High-risk AI must allow effective human oversight during period of use.
EU AI Act Article 15 accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity: High-risk AI must be accurate, robust, secure.
EU AI Act Article 17 quality management: Providers must implement quality management system.
EU AI Act Article 72 post-market monitoring: Providers must establish and document post-market monitoring system proportionate to nature of AI system.
EU AI Act penalty: Up to €35M or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited AI violations.
EU AI Act deadline: 2 August 2026 — most provisions apply.

NCSC SC-01 Cyber Assessment Framework: 14 controls covering security governance, risk management, asset management, supply chain, service protection, identity, cryptography, data security, system security, network security, staff awareness, malware protection, vulnerability management, incident management.
DSP SC2 Security Clearance: Required for handling SECRET material. Must be sponsored, have residency requirement, undergo Developed Vetting (DV) or Security Check (SC) clearance.
DSP SC1: Baseline Personnel Security Standard. Required for contractors with occasional access to government assets.
UK Cyber Essentials: 5 controls — firewalls, secure configuration, user access control, malware protection, patch management. Required for UK government contracts.
UK Section 7 OSA: Official Secrets Act 1989 — protects 7 categories of official information.
